title: Antidotes & Reversal Agents
sources: Critical Vector — Antidotes & Reversal Agents pocket reference (v7, verified against FDA / NEJM / MHAUS / ASRA / ACEP / AAP / poison-center references, July 2026)
Consult a medical toxicologist / regional poison center for any real poisoning

changelog.change: Initial entry — converted from the CV antidotes pocket reference: anaphylaxis/shock, sedation/opioid/NMB reversal, poison-induced cardiogenic shock ladder, toxidrome rescue, anesthesia emergencies, antidote-by-substance, chelation & metabolic rescue, envenomation. Adult doses in-line; selected peds doses called out.

summary: Every antidote that changes an outcome — indication, adult dose, one pearl. An antidote reverses a mechanism, not a patient: ask (1) is reversal actually indicated or is supportive care enough, (2) does reversing create a new problem, (3) how long does the antidote last vs the drug it reverses. That third question causes the 3am bounce-back. Anticoagulant reversal lives in the separate anticoagulation-reversal module.

body.text: Doses here are for reasoning and rapid recall, not a substitute for a poison-center or toxicology consult on a live case. Most antidotes need ongoing monitoring for recurrence, rebound, or a second wave of toxicity as the antidote clears faster than the poison.

items: Epinephrine (anaphylaxis): 0.3–0.5 mg IM (1 mg/mL) anterolateral thigh, repeat q5–15 min; start an IV infusion for refractory disease rather than stacking IM doses. IM, not SC. Antihistamines / steroids treat itch and the late phase — not the airway or the BP; don't let them delay epinephrine. Peds: 0.01 mg/kg IM (max ~0.3–0.5 mg); auto-injector 0.15 mg for 15–30 kg, 0.3 mg for > 30 kg — prefer a weight-based manual dose under 15 kg.
Glucagon: the rescue for anaphylaxis not responding to epinephrine in a patient on chronic beta-blocker therapy (beta-blockade blunts epinephrine's effect). Bolus then infusion.

rows: 0.04–0.4 mg IV, titrate to breathing (not full waking)
Short half-life — watch for re-narcotization; infusion for long-acting opioids. In dependence, full reversal IS the adverse event (precipitated withdrawal). Peds ≤ 5 y / 20 kg: 0.1 mg/kg/dose.
0.2 mg IV, repeat to max ~1 mg

NOT reflexive in undifferentiated overdose. Antagonizes the benzo's own anticonvulsant effect — unmasks seizures from co-ingested proconvulsants (TCAs: found in 42% of flumazenil-seizure cases). Avoid in chronic benzo use, seizure history, mixed/unknown ingestion.

body.text: Naloxone is low-risk and reasonable to trial; flumazenil is not.

rows: 2 mg/kg moderate block · 4 mg/kg deep block · 16 mg/kg immediate reversal post-intubation
Restored TOF ≥ 0.9 within 5 min in 98% vs 11% with neostigmine (deep block). Same mg/kg in peds (studied to birth). Keep monitoring after redosing.
Only works once spontaneous recovery has reached T2 — useless in deep block. Check TOF before choosing the agent, not after extubation.

body.text: Poison-induced cardiogenic shock — an escalating ladder

Beta-blocker, calcium-channel-blocker, and sodium-channel-blocker (TCA and related) overdoses converge on bradycardia + hypotension + a dying myocardium and share an antidote ladder rather than one fix.

rows: QRS widening from Na-channel blockade (TCA, also citalopram, cocaine, flecainide, diphenhydramine, hydroxychloroquine)
1 mEq/kg IV bolus (0.5–3), then infusion to target pH 7.50–7.55
Treat the QRS, not the acidosis — give it for QRS widening even without acidemia; stop once the QRS narrows. Peds < 2 y: use dilute 4.2% solution.
Chloride ≈ 3× elemental calcium of equal-volume gluconate but more caustic — give centrally. Peds: gluconate 60–100 mg/kg/dose
For hyperkalemia, calcium stabilizes the membrane but doesn't shift K⁺ — add albuterol + insulin/dextrose.
Bolus then infusion. Peds 0.05–0.15 mg/kg IV over 1–2 min
Drives cAMP through a separate G-protein pathway — works with the receptor fully occupied. Chronically under-dosed and under-lasting; won't carry a severe overdose alone.
Regular insulin ~1 U/kg bolus, then 0.5–1 U/kg/h (higher in refractory cases) + concentrated dextrose (≥ 20%) + frequent glucose/K⁺ checks

Increasingly FIRST-LINE at tox-experienced centers, not a last resort — the old 'glucagon, then calcium, then maybe insulin' undersells how early HIE should start. Watch for delayed hypoglycemia after weaning.

body.text: Serotonin syndrome develops over hours with hyperreflexia, clonus, tremor (neuromuscular hyperactivity); NMS develops over days with rigidity and sluggish reflexes (hypoactivity).

rows: Serotonin syndrome not controlled by drug cessation + benzos + supportive care
12 mg PO/NG load, then 2 mg q2h to response (~32 mg/day). Tablet only — crush for NG
Adjunct, not a substitute for stopping the serotonergic agents. Evidence inconclusive.
2.5 mg NG/PO q6–8h, uptitrate. Enteral only — no IV
Untreated NMS mortality ~21% → ~8% with dantrolene or bromocriptine alone; combination trends better. Prothrombotic (VTE prophylaxis).
Acute dystonic reaction (antipsychotics, metoclopramide, prochlorperazine) — minutes, not days
Benztropine 1–2 mg IV/IM, or diphenhydramine 25–50 mg IV/IM. Peds: diphenhydramine 1 mg/kg (max 50 mg)
Restores dopamine–ACh balance. Don't confuse a dystonic reaction (alert, frightened, posturing) with NMS (days, fever, rigidity, altered consciousness).

body.text: Dantrolene is also used off-label in NMS (see below).

rows: Malignant hyperthermia (+ stop triggers, 100% O2, active cooling)
2.5 mg/kg IV push q5–10 min to ~10 mg/kg (some need 20); maintenance 1 mg/kg q4–6h ≥ 24 h. Identical mg/kg at all ages (MHAUS)
Recrudescence in ~20%, median 8.7 h, 80% by 16 h — keep watching. Reconstitution is slow; call for hands early and know where it's stocked.
< 70 kg: 1.5 mL/kg bolus over 2–3 min → 0.25 mL/kg/min. > 70 kg: 100 mL bolus → 250 mL over 15–20 min. Repeat bolus / double infusion if unstable. Max ~12 mL/kg
ASRA 2020: benzodiazepines (not propofol) for LAST seizures; for arrest reduce epinephrine to < 1 mcg/kg boluses, avoid vasopressin / CCB / beta-blockers / other local anesthetics.

Atropine in doubling doses until secretions dry (atropinize to clear lungs, not to dilated pupils); pralidoxime per weight protocol before the enzyme ages. Peds atropine 0.02–0.05 mg/kg — the 0.1 mg minimum does NOT apply here.
0.5–1 mg IV/IM over 5–10 min, may repeat. AVOID if TCA cardiotoxicity (wide QRS) — can precipitate seizures / asystole. Reserve for clear anticholinergic delirium without conduction abnormality.

Weight-based PO or 3-bag IV protocol, guided by the Rumack-Matthew nomogram (level ≥ 4 h post-ingestion). ~100% hepatoprotective if started < 8 h; still helps after 24 h or in established failure. Start empirically if timing unknown or > 8 h.

By ingested amount or steady-state level. Thresholds: acute ≥ 10 mg or level ≥ 10 ng/mL; chronic toxicity with instability, refractory bradyarrhythmia, or K⁺ > 5.0–5.5. Treat the rhythm and the K⁺, not the post-Fab level (unreliable for days).
~15 mg/kg/hr infusion; consider at serum iron ≥ 350 mcg/dL with symptoms or ≥ 500 regardless. Watch for hypotension (free iron is a vasodilator). Disproportionately a toddler ingestion.

Succimer 10 mg/kg q8h ×5 d then q12h ×14 d for BLL > 45 (child) / > 80 (adult). Encephalopathy: dimercaprol FIRST, then CaEDTA 4 h later (EDTA before dimercaprol can mobilize lead INTO the brain). Note: dimercaprol no longer manufactured in the US since 2023 — succimer or CaEDTA monotherapy + tox consult.
Gram-for-gram with the ingestion if known; up to 5 g IV empiric. INH starves GABA synthesis, so benzos underperform until pyridoxine restores the substrate.
15 mg (or 10 mg/m²) IV/PO q6h, start as soon as toxicity is recognized; escalate to glucarpidase for severe toxicity with renal dysfunction. The longer MTX sits intracellularly, the harder to rescue.
IV load + infusion (optimal dose unsettled; IV preferred — oral bioavailability 14–18%). Valproate depletes carnitine needed for the fatty-acid metabolism that keeps ammonia detox running.
~1 mcg/kg SC/IV q6h alongside dextrose. Suppresses endogenous insulin, breaking the dextrose→insulin→hypoglycemia cycle. NOT for exogenous insulin overdose (sustained dextrose is the mainstay there).

1–2 mg/kg IV over 5 min, repeat in 1 h if MetHb > 30%. AVOID in G6PD deficiency (fails and worsens hemolysis); MAO-A inhibitor → serotonin syndrome risk on SSRIs. Infant Heinz-body hemolysis reported at doses as low as 4 mg/kg.

Non-rebreather immediately (cuts CO half-life ~4–6 h → ~1 h), continue until COHb ~3% and ≥ 6 h. HBOT is genuinely contested (Weaver 2002 favored it; Scheinkestel 1999 did not) — consider for LOC, COHb > 25%, pregnancy, or neuro/cardiac findings; don't delay stabilization hunting for a chamber.
5 g IV (peds 70 mg/kg, max 5 g). Think of it in enclosed-space smoke inhalation with unexplained lactic acidosis. Avoid nitrite-based kits in smoke inhalation (adds MetHb to a CO-loaded patient).

15 mg/kg load, then 10 mg/kg q12h ×4, then 15 mg/kg q12h until levels clear (adjust around dialysis). Blocks alcohol dehydrogenase before toxic metabolites form. Adverse events 12% vs 57% with ethanol — first-line where stocked.

body.text: Antivenom is dosed to neutralize a venom load, not scaled to patient size — a small child gets the same vial count as an adult with a comparable bite.

rows: North American pit viper (rattlesnake, copperhead, cottonmouth)
~4 vials copperhead, 6–12 rattlesnake, up to 12-vial initial max; repeat to control per protocol
NOT one-and-done. Recurrent / delayed coagulopathy is common, mostly in patients who missed maintenance dosing — recheck coagulation for days before any procedure or discharge.
Black widow, severe systemic symptoms not controlled by calcium + benzos + opioids
Latrodectism is painful but rarely fatal; equine antivenom carries real anaphylaxis / serum-sickness risk — reserve for severe or refractory cases.
Scorpion envenomation with cranial-nerve / neuromuscular signs (Arizona bark scorpion)
3 vials IV over 10 min, then 1 vial q30–60 min if symptoms persist
Mean time to resolution ~1.4 h. The country-of-origin protocol uses 1 vial with watchful waiting at comparable outcomes — expect a toxicologist to push toward a lower starting dose.
Foodborne, wound, adult intestinal botulism / infant botulism (< 1 y)
Via CDC or state health department (adult); BabyBIG 50 mg/kg IV via the California Infant Botulism Treatment Program (infant, any state)
Neutralizes only circulating unbound toxin — halts progression, does not reverse established paralysis. Treat on clinical suspicion; don't request heptavalent for a suspected infant case.

body.text: Protamine (heparin / LMWH), vitamin K + 4F-PCC (warfarin), idarucizumab (dabigatran), the post-2025 factor Xa inhibitor reversal picture, TEG/ROTEM interpretation, and the PATCH data on antiplatelet ICH all live in the anticoagulation-reversal module — not duplicated here so both stay accurate as guidance changes. Pediatric anticoagulant reversal is a separate lookup — don't extrapolate adult fixed-dose regimens onto a child.
